result.title: Self-Improving Agents with World Model Predictive Paths
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to interact with environments and improve their decisions during deployment. However, how anticipating future outcomes and drawing on accumulated interaction experience can jointly support decision-making remains underexplored. We propose a test-time framework, inspired by Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control, that combines multi-branch predictive analysis with experience-based adaptation. At each step, the agent proposes multiple candidate actions and imagines their outcomes with a world model, so that alternatives can be compared without being executed in the environment. Since language environments provide neither explicit dynamics nor costs, the predicted outcomes are evaluated for task progress and risk, and MPPI-style weights over the resulting costs guide the final decision. A dual-branch experience memory enables self-improvement: the planner branch refines candidate generation and action selection, while the world model branch improves next-observation prediction. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld across three backbones demonstrate the strong overall performance of our method and the effectiveness of experience-guided predictive control. Our code will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出借鉴 MPPI 控制的测试时 agent 框架：每步生成多个候选动作并用世界模型想象其结果，按任务进展与风险评分加权做出决策，并以双分支经验记忆分别改进候选规划与下一观测预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「想象多分支结果＋代价加权选择」与经验记忆式自我改进，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的候选生成、验证与信用分配提供方法线索；但环境与任务均为纯文本 agent，向视觉证据筛选的迁移可供核查。
